source_refs.quoted_text:
## Scientific target

The scientific target of this analysis is defined explicitly and only as the
retained post-screening subset of 18 eligible trap-nights. All claims below
apply to that retained subset, not to the complete planned set of 24
trap-nights.

evidence.description: The selected result's claim wording matches its denominator: a rate among the 18 retained trap-nights, computed as 7/18. I verified from the data that 3 nights have equipment faults (TN09, TN17, TN23) and 3 fault-free nights fall below 10.0 C (TN04, TN13, TN21), leaving 18 retained, of which 7 (TN01, TN03, TN07, TN11, TN15, TN19, TN22) recorded captures.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Among the 18 retained eligible trap-nights, 7 recorded at least one hawkmoth (Sphingidae) capture, a capture rate of 7/18 = 0.3889.

This capture rate uses the retained post-screening subset (n = 18) as its
denominator and makes no claim about the 6 screened-out trap-nights or about
the complete planned set of 24 trap-nights.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to show the issue is present by searching the report for any sentence that extends the 7/18 rate to the complete planned set of 24 trap-nights; every scope statement instead restricts the claim to the 18 retained units and explicitly disclaims the planned set. I also recomputed the accounting from the raw data to check for a hidden mismatch: 24 rows, 6 removed (TN04, TN09, TN13, TN17, TN21, TN23 by fault or minimum temperature below 10.0 C), 18 retained, 7 captures among retained (TN17's capture correctly excluded), and 7/18 = 0.3889 as reported. The task itself designates the retained subset as the target, so the subset denominator matches the declared domain and the issue class cannot be demonstrated.
